clue.text: Spot the infiltrator

definitions.meaning: a small dark blemish on the skin, a beauty mark
a spy planted inside an organisation, working for the other side

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a skin blemish and a double agent who burrows into an organisation.

clue.text: He can't speak for the dog!

parts.note: he refers to a male
someone who cannot speak is mute

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a man is too tongue-tied to talk on behalf of his dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The malemute is an Alaskan sled dog breed, also spelt malamute.

clue.text: Access Internet organisation's symbol and name

parts.note: a company's emblem is its logo

explanation.surface: Getting at an online organisation's emblem and name.
explanation.definitionFit: To log on is to connect to a computer system or network by signing in.

clue.text: Source of warm covering letter from abroad introducing Pulp

indicators.note: the letter comes first, introducing the next piece, so it stands at the front

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to pulp something is to squash it

explanation.surface: A foreign letter introduces the band Pulp and keeps someone warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulp' looks like the Britpop band but is the verb meaning to crush. A musquash is a muskrat, whose fur makes coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Musquash is muskrat fur, a pelt once widely used for warm coats.

clue.text: Order, after last of gateau's left over

indicators.note: the word for order is placed after the single letter
only the final letter of the word gateau's is taken

parts.note: to neaten is to put in order, tidy

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up after the last of the cake has been left uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that was never eaten is what remains on the plate as leftovers.

clue.text: Like McGraw's animator, wasting no time here?

definitions.text: Like McGraw's animator, wasting no time here?

parts.words: Like McGraw's animator, wasting no time here?
parts.note: the cartoon horse Quick Draw McGraw needs an artist who draws him, and a person who reacts instantly is fast to draw a gun

explanation.surface: A remark about how fast the artist behind a cartoon character works.
explanation.walkthrough: Quick Draw McGraw was a Hanna-Barbera cartoon horse who was a sheriff in the Wild West; his animator 'draws' him.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fast to pull a gun from its holster has become an idiom for reacting rapidly.

clue.text: Inventor making electrical discharge appropriate for listeners

indicators.note: the pieces are judged by how they would sound to anyone hearing them spoken

parts.note: an arc is a spark jumping between electrodes; right means fitting or proper

explanation.surface: An inventor creating an electrical spark suited to people listening.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Arkwright invented the water frame, a spinning machine of the Industrial Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright was an eighteenth-century English industrialist who devised cotton-spinning machinery.

clue.text: Dislike that everyone harbours

indicators.note: the phrase that everyone holds the letters within it, as a harbour shelters boats

explanation.surface: An aversion that every person secretly holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong dislike is loathing, the same feeling.

clue.text: Public availability secured by military ransom?

definitions.meaning: a film or product being made widely available to everyone
freeing a senior army officer could be what a ransom buys

explanation.definitionFit: A film on wide distribution is in cinemas everywhere, and paying for a captured army commander frees him.

clue.text: Facetious US soldier companies locked up

indicators.note: the companies are imprisoned within the soldier, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: GI Joe, so Joe is slang for an American soldier
COS is the plural abbreviation of company

explanation.surface: A joking American serviceman has firms put behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose describes someone playful and humorous, given to joking.

clue.text: Out on a limb?

parts.note: a cricket dismissal when the ball strikes the batsman's leg rather than the bat

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in a precarious position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out on a limb' is an idiom for being exposed, but in cricket a batsman can be given out when the ball hits the leg in front of the stumps: LBW.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket dismissal is decided by the ball hitting a batsman's leg, the limb, when it would have hit the stumps.

clue.text: Person with produce provides vegetable

parts.note: man means a person
to get out a book or product is to produce it

explanation.surface: A grower brings his produce to market and supplies vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangetout is a pea pod eaten whole, a type of green vegetable.

clue.text: Euro-Asian alcoholic turning over new leaves?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for new departs, taken out of the reversed word
the word for the drinker is flipped so it reads backwards

parts.note: a drunk is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker resolves to reform, turning over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' makes KNURD, and 'leaves' takes out the N for 'new'. The Kurds live where Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria meet, straddling Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kurdish people inhabit a region spanning south-eastern Turkey and western Asia.

clue.text: Worried after trial, not unwilling?

indicators.note: the word for worried follows the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
ate as in what is eating you, troubled

explanation.surface: Someone anxious after a court case, yet not reluctant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unwilling' looks like 'willing', but it means 'not without a will'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dying testate has left a valid legal will.

clue.text: Way idiot is landing

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
an airhead is a foolish person

explanation.surface: Some route an idiot is touching down on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairhead is the platform at the top of a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Everyone remains unconscious?

parts.note: read as nobody departs, and also the psychological term for what lies outside the conscious self

explanation.surface: A whole group stays knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NONE GO, 'everyone remains' is a fair reading: nobody leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy the non-ego is everything outside the conscious self, including the unconscious.

clue.text: Loves Wendy and Grace, for example

definitions.meaning: Wendy from Peter Pan and Grace, the lighthouse heroine, share a surname

explanation.definitionFit: Sweethearts are called dears; Wendy Darling is Peter Pan's friend and Grace Darling was a Victorian rescuer at sea.

clue.text: More than just this sex for women?

definitions.meaning: the old phrase calling women the fair sex

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just, so its comparative is more equitable, and the phrase 'the fairer sex' once meant women.

clue.text: Lots of cold water sprinkled, as with roses

indicators.note: scattering the letters as from a watering can mixes them up

explanation.surface: Plenty of chilly water scattered over roses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica.

clue.text: Sage mum used to cover pork-pie?

indicators.note: the mother goes around the hat, enclosing it

parts.note: mama is mother
a pork-pie is a flat-topped felt hat

explanation.surface: Mum once kept a pork pie covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork-pie' looks like food, but it is a style of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an honorific for a revered wise person in India, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Bad feeling from African country church

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Resentment arising from an African nation's church.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, the wish to harm someone.

clue.text: Examination of old

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Examination of old (4)' for ORAL: 'of old' gives no letters or sense for ORAL; probably an OCR misreading (perhaps of 'mouth'), not found by search and there is no scan.

clue.text: Allows bad ingredients in food dish

indicators.note: the letters are like ingredients being mixed together into something new

explanation.surface: A recipe allows poor ingredients in a dish of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad bowl is the wide dish in which a salad is tossed and served.

clue.text: Widespread negative reaction in old music-hall, audibly

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than read, giving a near-identical sound

parts.note: an odeum was an ancient Greek or Roman building for musical performance

explanation.surface: Booing in a Victorian music hall that everyone could hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust felt towards someone.

clue.text: A breeding-ground not miles distant

indicators.note: the miles abbreviation is excluded from the farm word

parts.note: a farm is where animals are bred

explanation.surface: A stud farm that is only a short way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great remove, far away.

clue.text: Technique available to shrink a club with no membership charge?

definitions.meaning: a method a psychiatrist (shrink) uses, the patient saying whatever comes to mind

definitions.text: a club with no membership charge?
definitions.meaning: a society that costs nothing to join

explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysts let patients voice unfiltered thoughts, and a society with no fees costs nothing to join.

clue.text: Tree Edward planted in Northern town

indicators.note: Edward is set inside the town, as a sapling is put in the ground

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward plants a tree in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcar is a seaside town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The western red cedar is a large North American conifer.

clue.text: Here is old prophet taking back the perfect drug

indicators.note: the drug's name is run in reverse

parts.note: soma is the ideal happiness drug in Huxley's Brave New World

explanation.surface: An ancient seer takes back the ideal narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Soma is the drug in Aldous Huxley's novel Brave New World. Amos is a minor prophet of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the Hebrew Bible's minor prophets, from the eighth century BC.
